prompt: It is now common for people to change careers several times during their working lives. Why is this happening? Do you think it is a positive or a negative development?
essay:
A working life spent in a single occupation, once the norm, is now unusual in most developed economies. The shift has both an external cause and an internal one, and although it imposes real costs on individuals, I regard it overall as a positive development.

The external cause is that occupations themselves are less stable than they were. Automation and offshoring have removed whole categories of clerical, manufacturing and administrative work within a single generation, and the industries replacing them require different skills rather than the same skills applied elsewhere. Somebody whose trade disappears at forty does not choose to retrain; the alternative is unemployment.

The internal cause is a change in what people expect from work. Where a previous generation valued security above almost everything, many workers now treat a job as something that ought to develop them, and they are far more willing to leave when it stops doing so. The growth of flexible online study has made acting on that impulse realistic, since a qualification can be acquired alongside existing employment rather than instead of it.

The costs are obvious enough. Changing field usually means a drop in earnings and in seniority, and the permanent possibility of change is a source of anxiety, particularly for those with dependants or mortgages. But the alternative was never security for everyone; it was security for those whose industry happened to survive. A workforce that expects to retrain absorbs technological change far better than one built around jobs for life, and individuals who can move are less trapped by a single employer than those who cannot.

On balance, then, the development is positive, provided that governments treat retraining as a normal stage of a career rather than as emergency relief for the unlucky.
title: Why people now change careers several times
